decision.title: A bound on evaluation steps (P9 accepted)

body.p: (orchestrator accepted P9, with "0 means sxml's default"). uint64_t maximum_evaluation_step_count in sxml_processor_limits; 0 means SXML_EVALUATOR_DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_EVALUATION_STEP_COUNT, 10^9 steps (about a minute of work, far beyond any QT4 test). sxml_evaluator_configuration has the same field with 0 meaning no bound. The machine charges one step per task run; sxml_dynamic_context_charge_steps lets leaf work charge what it reads: a general comparison charges the product of its operand counts first (O(1) for ranges), so -1 = -100000000000 to -1 stops at once, even though an early match would have ended it (the price of charging up front). The count restarts with every evaluation; past the bound, LIMIT_EXCEEDED with the diagnostic filled. Native bodies that loop over many items without tasks (fn:count, fn:string-join, sorting, regex) do not charge yet; each can call the function when needed. xpath_evaluate_fuzz sets 10^7 steps.
